recent_posts.title: How an engineer accidentally deleted the matrix.org production database
recent_posts.summary: Element Creations experienced a 24-hour outage of the matrix.org home server after an engineer accidentally deleted the production database while attempting to restore a failed server. The incident began with a hardware failure requiring database migration, but confusion over which server was primary led to running a destructive command on the wrong machine. Recovery took over a day due to slow backup restoration (51TB), a bug in their backup tool that wasn't patched in production, and slow write-ahead log replay. The postmortem emphasizes faster backup restoration strategies, including local snapshots using copy-on-write filesystems like ZFS, and highlights how operational errors during high-pressure situations are nearly inevitable.

recent_posts.title: How a bash script deployment error deleted 77TB at Kyoto University
recent_posts.summary: A detailed technical breakdown of how a backup script at Kyoto University accidentally deleted 77 terabytes of research data. The incident occurred when HP Enterprise deployed a script update using an in-place file modification (cp) instead of an atomic swap (mv), causing bash to execute a mix of old and new code. This resulted in an undefined variable being interpreted as an empty string, making the deletion command target the root directory instead of the intended log folder. The post explains file descriptors, inodes, atomic operations, and bash's line-by-line interpretation behavior, ultimately demonstrating why proper deployment practices and bash safety flags are critical.

recent_posts.title: How Kings College London lost everything when one server failed
recent_posts.summary: Kings College London experienced a catastrophic data loss in 2016 when their HP 3PAR storage system failed during a routine hardware replacement. A firmware incompatibility between the new controller node and existing hardware caused multiple disk failures, resulting in complete data loss. The incident exposed critical flaws in their backup strategy: volume snapshots were stored on the same failing machine, tape backups were fundamentally broken with regular automation failures, and disaster recovery testing was never performed. The recovery process took weeks and involved forensic data recovery, with some research data lost permanently. The failure highlighted the importance of proper backup redundancy, regular testing, and avoiding single points of failure in enterprise storage systems.

recent_posts.title: Canada's July 2022 internet outage: causes and consequences
recent_posts.summary: On July 8th, 2022, Rogers, one of Canada's major telecommunications providers, experienced a massive outage that affected internet, mobile services, and debit transactions nationwide for over 12 hours. The outage was attributed to a server upgrade mistake resulting in a flood of routing information, causing core routers to crash. The lack of redundancy and communication among Rogers staff exacerbated the situation. In response, Rogers committed to improving its infrastructure to prevent future occurrences.

recent_posts.title: Slack outage reveals autoscaling and load-balancing issues
recent_posts.summary: On May 12, 2020, Slack experienced a severe outage that highlighted issues in their autoscaling and load-balancing infrastructure. A buggy deployment led to increased load, which triggered an overenthusiastic autoscale of webapp instances. This overwhelmed the HAProxy load balancer, leading to uneven load distribution and server overloads. The engineers resolved the issue by understanding the autoscaling bug and restarting HAProxy instances, later deciding to replace HAProxy with Envoy Proxy for better reliability.

recent_posts.title: Incident Analysis: How a Bash Script Failure Caused Global Latencies at Cloudflare
recent_posts.summary: On December 16, 2021, Cloudflare faced a major incident during a rollback deployment which led to widespread high latencies. The issue was traced back to a bash script within a Kubernetes cron job that failed, resulting in an empty key in Cloudflare’s key-value store Quicksilver. This in turn caused the dosd service, responsible for analyzing traffic and providing attack fingerprints, to enter a crash loop. The cascading failures highlighted multiple areas for improvement, including stricter error handling in bash scripts, better failover mechanisms, and scaling of API services to handle peak loads during deployments.
